newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland Fed's median CPI up 0.2 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland Fed's median CPI up 0.2 pct in July.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland said on Thursday its median Consumer Price Index rose 0.2 percent in July versus up 0.2 percent in June.
Year-over-year, the median CPI was up 2.7 percent in July versus up 2.8 percent in June.

The Cleveland Fed's median CPI is a core measure of inflation that excludes all items that markedly depart from the median performance. It is calculated on the inflation data computed by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).
The BLS' core CPI solely excludes food and energy. Earlier on Thursday, the BLS said both the July CPI and core CPI inched up 0.2 percent.
Year-over-year, the CPI was up 2.2 percent in July and up 2.3 percent in June, while the core CPI was up 2.4 percent versus up 2.5 percent.
